title: Counter-program simulation machine
statement: Let $R$ be a natural number, let $\Lambda$ be a type of labels, let $P$ assign a counter-program instruction to each label, and fix an initial label $l_0$ and a Boolean $lm$. Define a two-decider register machine with $R+3$ registers and the simulation labels as its states: it starts by validating the input, follows each counter-program instruction while using the extra registers to handle output and printing, calls the first decider on the unary-first virtual input for read instructions, and halts with the corresponding Boolean answer; a program halt or an instruction/state mismatch returns false.
hypotheses_covered: $P$ assigns an instruction to each label
caveat: The declaration depends on the meanings of counter-program instructions, virtual inputs, and decider calls, whose defining descriptions are not included in the supplied definitions.
